newsitem.title: UK: Britons sentenced for anti-Indonesia protest.
newsitem.headline: Britons sentenced for anti-Indonesia protest.

text.p: Two British peace activists who trepassed onto British Aerospace (BAe) property to protest at the export of Hawk missiles to Indonesia received three-month suspended jail sentences on Friday for contempt of court.

Ciaron O'Reilly of Liverpool and Stephen Hancock of Oxford admitted they had breached an injunction and buried a child's coffin on BAe land last December to bury in memory of East Timorese children who have died under Indonesian rule.
BAe signed a contract in June 1993 to supply 24 Hawk missiles to Indonesia.

"BAe is abetting genocide in East Timor," Hancock told the High Court. "And yet we are brought before this court for opposing this crime. The High Court is putting BAe's property rights before the lives of the people of East Timor."

The judge said no one could fail to be impressed by what the men had said in their defence, but they had defied an injuction banning them from trepassing on BAe property to draw attention to their campaign.
Indonesia took control of the former Portugese colony in 1975. Human rights groups say about 200,000 people died during the takeover and subsequent fighting and famine in East Timor.
